previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and polysubstance abuse was admitted for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, worsening dyspnea, and a syncopal episode. His heart failure exacerbation was attributed to poor medication absorption due to gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to fluid overload. He was treated with intravenous diuresis and transitioned back to oral torsemide, with improvement in respiratory status. A small deep vein thrombosis in the right lower extremity was identified, and anticoagulation was initiated with enoxaparin and warfarin. His viral gastroenteritis resolved with supportive care, and renal function stabilized. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions on medication management, weight monitoring, and follow-up for anticoagulation control.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ M with a history of heart failure 
(likely due to prior cocaine abuse, LVEF 15% ___, CKD III, 
restrictive lung disease (likely due to cocaine use), hepatitis 
C, schizophrenia, DM2, recent diagnosis of RLE DVT who presents 
with hematuria, s/p syncopal episode this admission, with 
dyspnea.
.
ACUTE ISSUES
#) Syncope
The patient had an unwitness syncopal episode during his 
admission. Prior to this episode, the patient  reported 2 other 
episodes of syncope. The syncopal episode took place as the 
patient was getting up to use the restroom and then fell. A CT 
head and CT C spine showed no fracture or acute process. 
However, he did suffer two loose teeth, #23 and #24, which were 
extracted by OMFS. Fall precautions were placed, and the patient 
had no further syncopal episodes. 
.
There was no clear precipitant for Mr. ___ syncopal episode. 
No events on telemetry and no post-cital period, bowel, or 
bladder incontinence to indicate seizure. The patient had 
evidence of pulmonary hypertension on last echo ___ and poor 
lung function at baseline due to restrictive lung disease, 
thought to be due to cocaine use. Thus pulmonary hypertension 
and hypoxemia was thought to be related to his syncopal 
episodes. A repeat cardiac echo showed an EF of 15% and moderate 
pulmonary hypertension that may be underestimated due to 4+ 
tricuspid regurgitation. 
.
The pulmonary team was consulted and felt that his worsening 
pulmonary hypertension was due to worsening left heart failure. 
They recommended diuresing the patient to his dry weight, 
weaning oxygen, and obtaining DLCO soon after discharge. 
.
#) HYPOXEMIA: 
The patient developed worsening hypoxemia s/p his syncopal 
episode. He has poor lung function at baseline as described 
above. His hypoxemia was likely multi-factorial related to 
decompensated heart failure, restrictive lung disease, and 
pulmonary hypertension. A CTA was negative for pulmonary 
embolism. CT C spine showed worsening opacification at the right 
apex for which he was started on levofloxacin for CAP. A 
legionella antigen was negative. The patient also received 
nebulizers and was diuresed with his home torsemide and 
furosemide. 
.
#)Tachycardia 
The patient developed worsening tachycardia s/p his syncopal 
episode. His baseline heart rate during his last admission was 
in the 100s likely due to his heart failure and poor lung 
function as described above. However his pulse increased to the 
___ s/p fall. This worsening tachycardia was likely due to 
hypovolemia due to diuresis, poor PO intake, and pain s/p fall. 
His cardiac enzymes were cycled and were negative. He received 
oxycodone for pain management, and nebulizers as above, with 
improvement in his tachycardia. 
.
# PNA
The patient was found to have worsening opacification at the 
right lung apex s/p fall on CT C spine. Given his worsening 
dyspnea and hypoxia, he was started on levofloxacin for HCAP 
which was completed prior to discharge. 
.
#)Hypotension 
The patient developed transient hypotension during admission, 
with SBP in the ___. He remained asymptomatic and was mentating 
normally. This hypotension was most likely ___ hypovolemia as 
patient had been NPO that morning, in addition to prior poor PO 
intake ___ mouth pain, and some blood loss ___ from the mouth. 
In addition, the patient had been diuresed the day prior to his 
hypotension.  Sepsis was less likely given that he had no 
leukocytosis and no fever. He responded well to fluid boluses 
with SBP in the 100s, and remained normotensive thereafter. 
.
#) HEMATURIA: 
The patient initially presented to the ED w/ gross hematuria. He 
had no further episodes of gross hematuria during admission, his 
UA was positive for 65 RBCs. A subsequent UA showed 5 RBCs.  
Although he was on anticoagulation, is abnormal. Fortunately, he 
did not exhibit hemodynamic instability on presentation and did 
not present with a significant drop in hematocrit (36% down from 
37% at prior discharge). Thus, he was continued on 
anticoagulation.  A renal U/S did not show evidence of stone. An 
initial urine cx was positive for alpha strep vs lactobacillus, 
likely contaminants. A subsequent urine cx showed no growth. An 
HIV test was negative during admission, and the patient had had 
recent gonorrhea and chlamydia testing which were both negative.
.
CHRONIC ISSUES
#) DVT: 
The patient was diagnosed with RLE DVT during his ___ 
admission. On this admission his INR was subtherapeutic. He was 
started on a heparin drip, and his warfarin was initially held 
in anticipation of his tooth extraction. The patient was 
discharged with warfarin and enoxaparin bridge. 
.
#) COPD: 
The patient has a known diagnosis of COPD. He was continued on 
his home nebulizers during admission. 
.
#) CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE, STAGE III: GFR ___. Baseline 
creatinine 1.5-1.7.  
The patient has a known diagnosis of CKD. His medications were 
renally dosed and he remained stable with regards to his kidney 
disease.  
.
#) HEART FAILURE:
As described above, the patient has a known diagnosis of heart 
failure, with an EF of 15%. He was continued on his home 
losartan, torsemide, and digoxin.  
.
#) DIABETES MELLITUS, TYPE 2:
The patient has a known diagnosis of DM2. He was continued on 
lantus at a lower dose than his home regimen given an episode of 
hypoglycemia during admission. His insulin sliding scale was 
also adjusted accordingly, without further episodes of 
hypoglycemia. 
.
#) ANXIETY: 
The patient has a known diagnosis of anxiety and was continued 
on his home benzodiazepines  
.
